scenario.human_factors: tourist posted, iwi members request removal but algorithm sees disagreement as conflict

events_timeline: Month 1: tourist posts "amazing rocks for photos"
Month 2: iwi rep reports as cultural violation, 3 supporting reports
Month 3: confused likes from other tourists "great spot"
Month 4: media attention, more reports from supporters
Month 15: 30 likes (mostly tourist), 18 reports (mostly cultural)
cases.expected_signal_summary: 30 likes, 18 reports — high report ratio with cultural authority
cases.human_judgment: Cultural-authority reports outweigh raw counts. Tourist likes are uninformed. Should sink.

cases.human_judgment: Mono-lingual marks are valid. Language barrier should not be treated as quality issue.

cases.title: Scenic mark obsolete after wildfire / natural disaster

scenario.intrinsic_quality: Was excellent until fire/storm destroyed scenery
scenario.human_factors: mark created pre-disaster has 80 historical likes; post-disaster visitors report as no longer accurate

events_timeline: Month 1-12: built up 80 likes pre-disaster
Month 13: wildfire destroys forest backdrop
Month 14-15: 12 reports "scenery no longer exists"
Month 16: original poster updates description
Month 18: 80 historical likes vs 18 post-disaster reports
cases.human_judgment: Historical likes don't reflect current reality. Recent reports should weigh more for environmental change. Algorithm needs recency weighting.
